subject: Taxes
title: The Technology Debt Crisis
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Technology Debt Crisis usable.

hook.text: The IRS Master File—the central database of every taxpayer—runs on code written in the 1960s.

buildup.text: COBOL programmers who built these systems have retired or died.

discovery.text: During COVID, the IRS literally couldn't process paper returns fast enough.

twist.text: Private-sector tax software companies have advanced far beyond IRS capabilities.

climax.text: The IRS's technology crisis isn't just inconvenient—it's a national security risk.

punchline.text: 1960s code, dead-language programmers, 35 million stuck returns.

quiz.question: What programming language does the IRS Master File still use?
